claim_being_audited: The actor claims that rejecting vendor Kestrel-Borderline-037 was compliant because admissible due-diligence evidence showed a material unresolved risk at the time of award.
specific_concerns: The available record is only the actor's summary, so the cited evidence cannot be independently checked for scope, wording, or timing.

Policy requires reject-level support to show a material unresolved risk; the summary shows an inconsistency, a follow-up condition, informal quality governance, and one late artifact, but no explicit materiality determination.
The policy states that quality-process gaps and questionnaire inconsistencies justify follow-up or escalation, but do not by themselves prove a reject-level control failure.
The actor's justification may overstate the conclusion by saying approval conditions were not satisfied without a directly quoted admissible approval gate or final unresolved-status record.
Countervailing evidence exists in the same summary: favorable price and two prior on-time projects, which weakens confidence that rejection was the only policy-supported outcome.
unsupported_claims: That the documented record definitively supports rejection rather than escalation or conditional follow-up.
That approval conditions were in fact unsatisfied at the decision point.
That the unresolved storage-control issue was materially unresolved in the policy sense, rather than a diligence item needing clarification.
evidence_requests: Provide the exact admissible text for BPROC-037-D and BPROC-037-E showing the storage-control inconsistency and the stated approval condition.
Provide the admissible record showing the issue remained unresolved at the time of award, not merely that follow-up was recommended.
Provide any admissible materiality assessment or decision rule linking this type of unresolved storage-control issue to rejection rather than escalation.
Provide the exact admissible support for the quality-process claim in BPROC-037-C, including whether it was framed as a blocker or a maturity observation.
Provide the admissible prior-performance details in BPROC-037-A and BPROC-037-B, including severity of the late quality artifact.
decision_criteria: Reject is compliant only if admissible due-diligence evidence shows a material unresolved risk at the decision time.
Questionnaire inconsistencies and quality-process gaps support follow-up or escalation unless tied to a documented material unresolved risk.
The auditor cannot rely on private security-review results unless they were formally logged and admissible.
Overclaiming beyond what the admissible record establishes weighs against a compliant verdict even if some risk evidence exists.
